rounds.text: Texmo Pipes & Products Ltd is trading at a compelling valuation of 11.6x P/E [E1] and a price-to-book ratio of 0.76x against a book value of ₹ 79.0 [E2], representing a steep discount to the sector benchmark P/E of 23.99x [E6] and sector P/B of 2.57x [E7]. This low multiple is paired with a strong fundamental valuation setup, as a discounted cash flow intrinsic value of ₹ 81 per share provides a margin of safety of 26.2% [E45, E46], and a reverse DCF shows the current price implies minimal earnings growth of just 0.7% [E47]. The balance sheet remains sound and conservatively financed with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.24x, borrowings reduced to ₹ 55 Cr from ₹ 64 Cr [E38, E40], and a comfortable short-term liquidity current ratio of 2.11x [E39]. Operational momentum is also visible, with TTM operating margins expanding by 3 percentage points over three years to 9% [E30], quarterly operating margin up 2 percentage points year-over-year to 10% [E31], and a rules-based screen scoring the stock 84 out of 100 on the back of 12% YoY sales growth and 23% YoY net profit growth [E64, E65, E66]. Furthermore, the company benefits from a supportive macro backdrop with the Capital Goods sector in a tailwind with a score of +1.04 [E71, E73], and the price sits above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages with a relative-strength rating of 100 [E50, E51]. Conceded: compounded sales growth has contracted over recent multi-year periods, including -16% over 3 years and -2% over 5 years [E15, E16], and cash conversion remains weak with operating cash flow at just 0.07x of reported profit for Mar 2026 [E34].

Texmo Pipes & Products Ltd exhibits severe top-line stagnation and long-term contraction, demonstrated by a compounded sales growth of -2% over 5 years and -16% over 3 years [E15, E16]. Profitability metrics are chronically weak, with a 3-year low return on equity of 6.53% [E62] and a 10-year median ROE of just 1% [E26]. Cash generation is deeply disconnected from reported accounting earnings; cash conversion for Mar 2026 stands at an alarming 0.07x, translating into a negative free cash flow of Rs -7 Cr alongside deteriorating debtor days that have stretched from 69.6 to 88.7 days [E34, E36, E63]. Furthermore, the company pays a dividend yield of 0.00% despite reporting repeated profits, offering no cash return to shareholders [E4, E60]. Compounded share price growth over 3 years is -5% [E24], and the stock carries an exceptionally high annualised volatility of 65.8% coupled with a poor Sharpe ratio of 0.23 [E54, E55]. Conceded: the company trades at a low price-to-book ratio of 0.76x and a P/E of 11.6x which sits well below sector benchmarks [E1, E2, E6].

Conceded: 3-year compounded sales growth is -16% [E16] and 5-year sales growth is -2% [E15]. Conceded: the 10-year median ROE is 1% [E26] and dividend yield is 0.00% [E4]. However, the bear ignores that profit growth has sharply decoupled from past top-line stagnation, delivering a 31% compounded profit growth over 3 years [E20] and a rules-based screen score of 84 out of 100 [E64]. Operating margins are expanding, reaching 9% in the TTM compared to 6% three years earlier [E30], and quarterly operating margin rose to 10% in June 2026 from 8% a year prior [E31]. Furthermore, debt has decreased to Rs 55 Cr from Rs 64 Cr a year earlier [E40], supporting a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.24x [E38] and a comfortable current ratio of 2.11x [E39]. Valuation multiples remain deeply discounted relative to the broader sector, with an EV/EBITDA of 5.65x against a sector benchmark of 14.16x [E11] and a P/E of 11.6x versus the sector's 23.99x [E6], while operating within a capital goods sector experiencing strong tailwinds [E71].

Conceded: 3-year compounded profit growth is 31% [E20], debt decreased to Rs 55 Cr [E40], debt-to-equity is 0.24x [E38], current ratio is 2.11x [E39], EV/EBITDA is 5.65x against a sector benchmark of 14.16x [E11], P/E is 11.6x against 23.99x [E6], and capital goods reads a tailwind score of +1.04 [E73]. However, the bull's reliance on profit growth ignores severe underlying cash generation failures, as operating cash flow was only 20% of operating profit and free cash flow turned negative at Rs -7 Cr in March 2026 [E36, E37]. The cash conversion ratio of 0.07x for March 2026 highlights that reported profits are running far ahead of actual cash, pointing directly to warning signs in receivables and accruals [E34]. Furthermore, debtor days have worsened significantly from 69.6 to 88.7 days [E63]. While the bull celebrates margin expansion and screen scores [E30, E31, E64], it glosses over the structural top-line decay including a 5-year sales contraction of -2% and a 3-year drop of -16% [E15, E16]. Finally, the stock trades at 100% of its 52-week range with an annualized volatility of 65.8% and a poor Sharpe ratio of 0.23 [E48, E54, E55].
